findings.title: Error IDs zipped positionally against nodestore get_multi values
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` by position. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id, and some backends only include found entries or return them in a different order. When that happens, error ids get attached to the wrong event payloads, or the list silently shifts. The data should be looked up by the generated node id, e.g. `events.get(node_id)` for each `(event_id, node_id)` pair.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared with rrweb event timestamps (likely milliseconds)
findings.body: Error `timestamp` comes from nodestore event data, which is in float seconds. It is compared directly against the top-level `event["timestamp"]` of replay recording events. rrweb recording events normally carry millisecond timestamps. If so, every error compares as earlier than the first recording event and is emitted at the start of the log, so the interleaving is wrong. The tests use seconds for both values, which hides the mismatch. The units should be normalized before comparing.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered when a search query is present
findings.body: When `searchQuery` is empty, the memo returns the full sorted list before the `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` filter runs. As a result `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown in the default view and are hidden only while the user is searching. The hidden-attribute filter should apply unconditionally.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty columns and data
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the widget renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`. It ignores `result.data` and `result.meta`, so every table widget for flagged orgs shows an empty table. The actual results should be converted into `TabularData` and columns.

findings.title: No-op migrations reference a 0921 migration not present in this change
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 were turned into no-ops with a comment pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py` as the correct migration. That migration is not part of this PR. If it does not exist, the org saved-search to view conversion is silently dropped and the comment is misleading. The comment's claim that 0920 "was never run" should also be verified for environments that may already have applied it.

findings.title: Mutual-exclusion check on age/timestamp uses truthiness
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `.get("timestamp")` by truthiness. A report with `age: 0` (valid per spec) plus `timestamp`, or `timestamp: 0` plus `age`, therefore passes even though it mixes both specs. Reports with neither field are also accepted, despite the docstrings saying one must be present. The check should use `"age" in self.initial_data` and enforce that exactly one of the two fields is provided.

findings.title: Container lost align-items/gap when replaced by Flex
findings.body: The old `Container` extended `FlexBox`, which set `align-items: center` and `gap: space(1)`. The replacement `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">` drops both, so the tabs and vitals are no longer vertically centered or spaced. A similar regression is in `traceWaterfall.tsx`, where the removed `FlexBox` set `height: 100%` and the new `Flex` does not.

findings.title: Query options dropped (retry/refetchOnWindowFocus) on attribute keys query
findings.body: The previous `useApiQuery` call set `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false`. The new `useQuery` uses the defaults instead, so failing attribute-key requests are retried several times and the query refetches on every window focus. This is a behavioral and load change that appears unintended.
